items.title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
items.summary_1line: Agents driven by large language models are increasingly deployed on long-horizon tasks, where they use tools and modify real workspaces. How well they perform depends as much on the harness around the model as on the...
items.why_it_matters: Matches feed focus: agent, harness, eval.
items.editor_note: Frames harness design as a first-class factor in coding-agent results.

items.title: ClueFlow: Learning Long-Horizon Search through Attributed Research-State Transitions
items.summary_1line: Long-horizon search requires agents to acquire relevant evidence and integrate it into an evolving research state. Existing methods maintain research states to guide exploration or assign turn-level progress signals,...
items.editor_note: Adds a method for learning search from attributed research-state transitions.

items.title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
items.summary_1line: Sparse outcome rewards make it difficult for long-horizon language-model agents to assign credit to earlier actions. Learned critics provide value estimates for intermediate states, but these estimates can be inaccura...
items.editor_note: Proposes active critic learning to improve credit assignment when critic estimates are inaccurate.

editorial.tldr: Doc2Harness opened the thread on Oct 14 by measuring how much the harness around a model, not just the model, drives long-horizon coding-agent results. Over the next week, papers added search-state learning (ClueFlow), error-recovery tests for computer-use agents (CUA-Recovery) and a continual-learning exam.
editorial.whats_new: FOCUS (Oct 26) proposes active critic learning to fix credit assignment under sparse outcome rewards, moving the thread from measuring long-horizon agents to training them.
editorial.why_it_matters: Long-horizon agent failures come from harness design, silent state corruption and weak credit assignment, so benchmarks that isolate those factors are more useful for platform decisions than single-score leaderboards.
editorial.take_for_builders: When evaluating a long-horizon agent, rerun it under your own harness and add an injected-error recovery case before trusting a leaderboard score.

status.detail: Five arXiv preprints, no independent replication yet; benchmarks and training methods are arriving together.

beats.headline: Doc2Harness benchmarks harness engineering for coding agents
Search state and computer-use error recovery get their own tests
Continual learning and critic training extend the focus to improvement over time

open_questions: Does any of these benchmarks get adopted by a major lab or independent evaluator?
Do the reported FOCUS gains hold on a third-party long-horizon benchmark?
Will CUA-Recovery results show shipped computer-use agents detecting silent state corruption?
